Representation level: L1 (proxy). CineRecon Three.js sampled-frame baseline (native inspect-revise protocol), not a Blender-equivalent reproduction.

Observed (from 24 reference samples, 1280x720, 23.976 fps, 501 frames): a dark bell-tower stair climb. A man in a dark suit with grey hair climbs a square wooden stairwell inside a stone tower; a woman in a grey suit with light hair appears in dark intercut shots. Shots include a high-angle look down (f0), a high-angle shot of the man climbing toward camera (f22-f43), medium shots beside a dark beam with a bright arched opening (f65-f87, f283-f304, f326-f348, f391-f435), two over-the-rail POV shots straight down the shaft (f109-f130 with hands on the rail and a dolly-zoom; f370 without hands), several very dark shots (f174-f239), a two-person shot (f261), a low-angle climb beside a diagonal rail (f457) and a low angle up the stairwell (f478-f500).

Geometry: stone tower (4 wall boxes, brick floor), 12 extruded stair flights in a clockwise square spiral around an open 2.2 m well, corner landings, sloped hand rails, four well-corner posts, arched bright window planes. Close-up shots use a small kit of flat wall/beam/arch proxies placed in each shot's base camera framing. People are articulated proxies (pelvis, two-segment legs, torso with shirt/tie strip, neck/head with hair cap, two-segment arms with hands); two-bone IK places hands on the rail (POV), at the face, and for reaches.

Camera and timing: 16 shots with hard cuts placed at midpoints between samples whose content changes; within shots, camera pans/tilts and subject motion are interpolated analytically between sampled states. The first POV uses an analytic dolly-zoom (FOV widens while the camera closes on the rail so hands stay constant and the shaft bottom shrinks). Letterbox bars of the source are reproduced as black camera-attached strips. update(time) is absolute and deterministic; seed is unused (no randomness).

Inference vs observation: exact cut frames, motion between samples, the identity of the figure in the darkest shots (f174, f196 assigned to the woman; f217, f239 to the man), and the tower layout are inferred.

Feedback: none received yet (initial round). Remaining uncertainties: lighting levels under the harness renderer, exact framing of tower shots (A, B, M, P), and the precise cut times.
